justification: Both surfaces combine a band of cuneiform text with carved figural imagery, but the specific content differs sharply: A shows a row of small deity/worshipper figures above a large inscription block on a weathered outdoor rock face, while B shows a single detailed eagle-headed winged genie beside a stylized palmette 'tree' beneath a narrow inscription band. The lack of any shared distinctive motif (no genie, no tree, no multiple deities in A; no rock-face setting or podium row in B) and the reversed placement of text relative to figures make the correspondence largely generic rather than iconographically specific.
